title: Maximum Matrix Sum
summary: Given an n x n integer matrix, you can perform the following operation any number of times: Choose any two adjacent elements of the matrix and multiply each by -1.
statement: Given an n x n integer matrix, you can perform the following operation any number of times: Choose any two adjacent elements of the matrix and multiply each by -1. Two elements are considered adjacent if they share a border. The goal is to maximize the sum of the matrix's elements. Return the maximum possible sum.
constraints: matrix is nonempty, square, and has side length at most 250.
One operation negates two orthogonally adjacent entries; operations may repeat.
Return the largest possible sum after any number of operations.
reference_solution:
def maximum_matrix_sum(matrix):
    absolute_sum = sum(abs(value) for row in matrix for value in row)
    negative_count = sum(value < 0 for row in matrix for value in row)
    smallest = min(abs(value) for row in matrix for value in row)
    return absolute_sum if negative_count % 2 == 0 else absolute_sum - 2 * smallest

hints: Pair negations let signs move through the connected grid, so only negative-count parity is invariant unless a zero absorbs it.
Take every absolute value; if parity is odd, leave the smallest magnitude negative.
Any even set of signs can be corrected through adjacent operations. Odd parity forces one negative, and choosing the smallest magnitude loses the least sum.
editorial: Any even set of signs can be corrected through adjacent operations. Odd parity forces one negative, and choosing the smallest magnitude loses the least sum.

tests.explanation: Two negatives have even parity, so all four magnitudes can contribute positively for a sum of four.
With odd negative parity, magnitude one must remain negative, giving eight.
